S3a integration experiment: owner review

Every image from the experiment, grouped by pair and prompt variant. The plan is identical within each pair; only the wording of the donor covering changes (V0 baseline to V5 growth by edit). Rate each image 1 to 5: integrated (does the donor covering grow out of the body with a natural transition, or sit on top as pieces), placement correct (where the plan puts it: back and flanks; belly and legs keep the host covering) and looks like a real animal. Ratings are kept in this browser while you work; use Export ratings to save them as JSON and send the file back. The critic results are the plan-blind protocol (two critics, describe first, balanced checklist).

Rhinoceros beetle x brown bear (speculative, bear host)

spark_open: The creature is a large quadrupedal mammal shown in right-facing profile against a plain light background. Its entire body except for several glossy dark structures is covered in dense, shaggy brown fur that is darker on the lower legs and lighter tan on the muzzle, chest and underside. It has the proportions and head shape of a bear, standing on four thick legs with clawed paws and a very short stubby tail at the rear. On its back are two large, smooth, highly glossy dark reddish-brown domed structures resembling beetle exoskeleton, one over the shoulders and a larger oval over the mid-back to rump. A single large glossy dark curved horn with a small side prong projects from the center of its forehead between the ears, and segmented glossy plates cover the outer sides of the forelegs. A row of small circular holes rims the lower edge of the larger back shell where it meets the fur.

meta_spark: A large bulky four-legged creature with dense shaggy brown bear fur covering its head, torso, legs and short tail, standing in profile facing right. It has a bear head with a tan muzzle, black nose, small dark eyes and small rounded ears, but with a single long curved glossy dark beetle horn growing from its forehead. On its back are two large glossy dark reddish-brown beetle shells, one shield-like plate over the shoulders and one long elytra-like shell over the rear back, with a row of small round holes along the furry flank beneath the rear shell. The upper front legs bear patches of glossy dark segmented beetle armor, and all four feet are broad bear paws with long pale claws.

Exact prompt
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a single curved horn of hard, glossy chitin rising from the brow; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, in a few large patches over the back and flanks, with clean edges, color and surface unchanged inside each patch. Coat texture and patches follow the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
